The concept of error correction involves the receiver using an error-correcting code that automatically corrects certain errors, a process known as forward error correction. These error-correcting codes are more advanced than error-detecting codes and necessitate the use of more redundant bits. To correct an error, it is essential to know the exact position of the error, meaning precisely which bit is erroneous, to locate the invalid bits.

Single-bit error correction is the simplest case to understand the broader concept of error correction. While a single-bit error can be detected by adding a parity bit (VRC) to the data, this single additional bit is insufficient to also correct the error. For correcting a single-bit error, such as in an ASCII character, the error correction mechanism must determine which specific bit among the data bits is incorrect, and this requires the addition of more redundant bits beyond what is needed for mere detection.
